title: This lint checks that no function newer than the defined MSRV (minimum supported rust version) is used in the crate.
summary: It would prevent the crate to be actually used with the specified MSRV. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Warns if an integral or floating-point constant is grouped inconsistently with underscores.
summary: Readers may incorrectly interpret inconsistently grouped digits. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for struct constructors where the order of the field init in the constructor is inconsistent with the order in the struct definition.
summary: Since the order of fields in a constructor doesn’t affect the resulted instance as the below example indicates, Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: The lint checks for slice bindings in patterns that are only used to access individual slice values.
summary: Accessing slice values using indices can lead to panics. Using refutable patterns can avoid these. Binding to individual values also improves the readability as they can be named. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of indexing or slicing that may panic at runtime.
summary: To avoid implicit panics from indexing and slicing. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for bit masks in comparisons which can be removed without changing the outcome.
summary: The basic structure can be seen in the following table: Not equally evil as bad_bit_mask, but still a bit misleading, because the bit mask is ineffective. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks if both .write(true) and .append(true) methods are called on a same OpenOptions.
summary: .append(true) already enables write(true), making this one superfluous. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of .to_string() on an &&T where T implements ToString directly (like &&str or &&String).
summary: In versions of the compiler before Rust 1.82.0, this bypasses the specialized implementation of ToString and instead goes through the more expensive string formatting facilities. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for matches being used to destructure a single-variant enum or tuple struct where a let will suffice.
summary: Just readability – let doesn’t nest, whereas a match does. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Finds manual impls of TryFrom with infallible error types.
summary: Infallible conversions should be implemented via From with the blanket conversion. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for iteration that is guaranteed to be infinite.
summary: While there may be places where this is acceptable (e.g., in event streams), in most cases this is simply an error. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for infinite loops in a function where the return type is not ! and lint accordingly.
summary: Making the return type ! serves as documentation that the function does not return. If the function is not intended to loop infinitely, then this lint may detect a bug. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the definition of inherent methods with a signature of to_string(&self) -> String.
summary: This method is also implicitly defined if a type implements the Display trait. As the functionality of Display is much more versatile, it should be preferred. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for the definition of inherent methods with a signature of to_string(&self) -> String and if the type implementing this method also implements the Display trait.
summary: This method is also implicitly defined if a type implements the Display trait. The less versatile inherent method will then shadow the implementation introduced by Display. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for tuple structs initialized with field syntax.
summary: It will however not lint if a base initializer is present. The lint will also ignore code in macros. This may be confusing to the uninitiated and adds no benefit as opposed to tuple initializers Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for items annotated with #[inline(always)], unless the annotated function is empty or simply panics.
summary: While there are valid uses of this annotation (and once you know when to use it, by all means allow this lint), it’s a common newbie-mistake to pepper one’s code with it. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of AT&T x86 assembly syntax.
summary: To enforce consistent use of Intel x86 assembly syntax. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of Intel x86 assembly syntax.
summary: To enforce consistent use of AT&T x86 assembly syntax. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for #[inline] on trait methods without bodies
summary: Only implementations of trait methods may be inlined. The inline attribute is ignored for trait methods without bodies. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks that module layout does not use inline modules.
summary: Inline test modules (anything annotated with #[cfg(test)]) are not linted. Having multiple module layout styles in a project can be confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Enforce that where bounds are used for all trait bounds.
summary: Enforce a single style throughout a codebase. Avoid uncertainty about whether a bound should be inline or out-of-line (i.e. a where bound). Avoid complex inline bounds, which could make a function declaration more difficult to read. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of inspect().for_each().
summary: It is the same as performing the computation inside inspect at the beginning of the closure in for_each. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of x >= y + 1 or x - 1 >= y (and <=) in a block
summary: Readability – better to use > y instead of >= y + 1. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for division of integers
summary: When outside of some very specific algorithms, integer division is very often a mistake because it discards the remainder. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the usage of division (/) and remainder (%) operations when performed on any integer types using the default Div and Rem trait implementations.
summary: In cryptographic contexts, division can result in timing sidechannel vulnerabilities, and needs to be replaced with constant-time code instead (e.g. Barrett reduction). Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for into_iter calls on references which should be replaced by iter or iter_mut.
summary: Readability. Calling into_iter on a reference will not move out its content into the resulting iterator, which is confusing. It is better just call iter or iter_mut directly. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: This is the opposite of the iter_without_into_iter lint.
summary: It looks for IntoIterator for (&|&mut) Type implementations without an inherent iter or iter_mut method on the type or on any of the types in its Deref chain. It’s not bad, but having them is idiomatic and allows the type to be used in iterator chains by just calling .iter(), instead of the more awkward <&Type>::into_iter or (&val).into_iter() syntax in case of ambiguity with another IntoIterator impl. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks regex creation (with Regex::new, RegexBuilder::new, or RegexSet::new) for correct regex syntax.
summary: This will lead to a runtime panic. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for comparisons where the relation is always either true or false, but where one side has been upcast so that the comparison is necessary.
summary: Only integer types are checked. An expression like let x : u8 = ...; (x as u32) > 300 will mistakenly imply that it is possible for x to be outside the range of u8. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for comparisons between integers, followed by subtracting the greater value from the lower one.
summary: This could result in an underflow and is most likely not what the user wants. If this was intended to be a saturated subtraction, consider using the saturating_sub method directly. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for invisible Unicode characters in the code.
summary: Having an invisible character in the code makes for all sorts of April fools, but otherwise is very much frowned upon. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.
